newsitem.title: USA: CSCE Coffee plunges to 2-1/2 week lows, funds sell.
newsitem.headline: CSCE Coffee plunges to 2-1/2 week lows, funds sell.

text.p: Heavy fund selling drove CSCE coffee futures to two-and-a-half-week lows on Monday amid weakening technicals and a let up of supply concerns, traders said.
May delivery plummeted 17.90 cents per lb as of 1333 EST, to 168.45, after ranging from 185.90 to 167.65. July was off 15.15, at 157.00 cents, while the remaining months were 5.80 to 7.00 lower.
Traders said downward momentum accelerated after the active May contract fell through key support levels at 179.00, then 175.00, triggering a series of sell-stops.
A build up in coffee stocks certified for delivery against the exchange and an anticipated increase in Green Coffee Association (GCA) stockpiles weighed on sentiment, they said.
The GCA will release its monthly inventory data due after today's close. Most dealers expected the February data to show a small rise in stocks of up to 100,000 60-kg.
In January, supplies of green coffee stored in U.S. warehouses rose by 15,000 60-kg bags to 1,342,000 bags, the GCA said.

Meanwhile, the CSCE reported after Friday's close certified coffee stocks grew for the seventh day in a row, reaching 44,983 60-kg bags as of March 13. There were an additional 27,946 bags pending grading, the exchange said.
